pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory apparatus and instruments? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory apparatus and instruments.

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory Safety? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory Safety.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory Safety.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory Safety.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory Safety.

4. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids, Bases and Indicators? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids, Bases and Indicators.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrical Energy? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrical Energy.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrical Energy.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrical Energy.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproductive System? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproductive System.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproductive System.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproductive System.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproductive System.

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Integrated Science and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory Safety and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory apparatus and instruments and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Mixtures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory apparatus and instruments.

2. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory Safety.

4. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

5. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids, Bases and Indicators.

6. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy.

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproductive System.

9. D — Ice melting to water

10. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. B — 100 °C

12. C — newton (N)

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Introduction to Integrated Science; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Laboratory Safety; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Laboratory apparatus and instruments; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Mixtures; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
